title: Directions
source: User-provided workbook photo, manually transcribed; illustrated direction translations suggested separately

entries.example: We have to cross the street.
entries.description: To go from one side to the other side

entries.example: You can see where you are on the map.
entries.description: A drawing that shows where streets and places are

entries.example: Take the second right.
entries.description: Number two in a row; or 1/60 of a minute

entries.example: Go straight on, then turn left.
entries.description: To keep walking forward, not left or right
To walk by a place without stopping
To keep walking forward, not left or right
To walk from one side of the road to the other
To go round a corner the opposite way from right
Turn into street number two on the side that is not left
Very near, just where the street turns
Until you get to: Walk ___ the church.
On the other side of the street, facing something
Right beside

entries.example: His son picked him up from the airport.
entries.description: A place where planes take off and land

entries.example: We have to change trains at Waterloo Station.
entries.description: To get off one railway ride and get on another one

entries.example: In Ireland, it rains most of the time.
entries.description: Nearly always, usually

entries.example: He put his ticket into his coat pocket.
entries.description: A small bag in your jeans or jacket

entries.example: Tortoises are slow animals.
entries.description: The opposite of fast

entries.example: He hoped to see his son somewhere.
entries.description: In some place, but you don't know where

entries.example: They went into London by underground.
entries.description: Trains that go under the city, for example in London

entries.example: We can meet on market square.
entries.description: An open place in the town centre where people sell things

entries.example: Then simply go ahead.
entries.description: Just, in an easy way: ___ go ahead.

entries.example: Who wrote the positive comment?
entries.description: What you write under a posting to say what you think

entries.example: You can comment on the postings.
entries.description: To write what you think under a posting

entries.example: You can give positive and negative feedback.
entries.description: What people tell you about how good or bad your work was

entries.example: She invited ten guests to dinner.
entries.description: A person you invite to your home or party

entries.example: We offer you three nights for the price of two.
entries.description: To ask if someone wants something you can give

entries.example: There is a new shopping centre opening.
entries.description: The first day when a new shop or place starts

entries.example: Write a positive comment.
entries.description: Good, the opposite of negative

entries.example: The restaurant got a bad review online.
entries.description: A text about how good or bad a film, book or restaurant is

entries.example: Luigi's pizza is the worst pizza ever!
entries.description: The opposite of the best

entries.example: I'm sorry to bother you.
entries.description: To disturb someone

entries.example: I saw her standing at the bus stop waiting for the bus to arrive.
entries.description: A place where you wait to get on a bus

entries.example: There's a big fountain at market square.
entries.description: Water shoots up into the air from it, in a park or square

entries.example: You can interrupt politely.
entries.description: To start talking when someone else is talking

entries.example: You should always ask politely and say please.
entries.description: In a nice way, saying please and thank you

entries.example: Turn left at the traffic lights.
entries.description: Red, yellow and green signals where streets cross
